svg.title: NAT and PAT: how private hosts share one public address
svg.desc: The router rewrites the source on the way out and remembers the swap in a table, so replies find their way back
svg.text: NAT and PAT: how private hosts share one public address
The router rewrites the source on the way out and remembers the swap in a table, so replies find their way back
PAT gives PC2 port 51001 so the two flows stay unique
Return packet arrives with dst 198.51.100.1:51001 → table lookup → rewritten to 192.168.1.11:51000.
Static PAT = port forwarding (the green row)
Inside / outside is about WHERE the host lives;
local / global is about WHO is looking at the address.
NAT swaps addresses · PAT also swaps ports so thousands of hosts share one public IP (the 'overload' keyword).
Outbound creates the table row; unsolicited inbound has no row → dropped, unless you add a static PAT row.
